clue.text: Nutty fruit

definitions.meaning: informally, someone nutty or crazy is said to be ...

explanation.surface: A description of some fruit that tastes of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy, matching nutty, and is also simply the plural of a yellow tropical fruit.

clue.text: Arouses into activity most effective New York tax collectors?

parts.note: the best is the most effective
the IRS, Internal Revenue Service, collects tax across the US including New York; the question mark flags the loose example

explanation.surface: Wondering whether New York's top tax men are what stirs people into action.
explanation.walkthrough: IRS is the US federal tax agency; New York stands in for America.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestir is to rouse or stir up, usually oneself, into action.

clue.text: Corner vendor stocks sauce

indicators.note: the phrase Corner vendor holds the letters inside it, as a shop stocks goods

explanation.surface: A shop on the corner keeps a bottled sauce in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks like a condiment but means cheek here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce and nerve both mean cheek or impudence, brazen boldness.

clue.text: Novel health and beauty resort with reputation rising daily

parts.note: novel means new
a spa is a health and beauty resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

explanation.surface: A new spa building its reputation every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns REP upwards to give PER. 'daily' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper published every day.

clue.text: Hush about US technology institute forger

indicators.note: the instruction to hush goes about, or around, the institute

parts.note: sh is the sound used to ask for hush
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Silence about a forger at an American technology institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter but means one who forges metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith works metal at a forge, hammering it into shape, so is literally a forger.

clue.text: Slick men's boundless cold, base debauchery

indicators.note: without bounds, so the outer letters of each of the words Slick and men's are dropped

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking man's lack of restraint described as cold, low-minded debauchery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundless' strips SLICK to LIC and MEN'S to EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence can mean excessive freedom of behaviour, i.e. licentiousness or dissolute conduct.

clue.text: Old army or unorthodox chief civil authority

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An old army or a maverick head of the civil government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges OLDARMYOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord mayor is the head of a city corporation such as London's, its leading civic official.

clue.text: Group of actors acquiring Oscar succeed with little effort

indicators.note: the group takes on, or acquires, the letter inside it

parts.note: the cast of a play is its group of actors
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors wins an Oscar without really trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests an award but is O.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to make progress easily, without much exertion, like a freewheeling bike.

clue.text: Difficult experience in the dark on moon area

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the dark comes first

parts.note: night is the dark
a mare is a dark plain on the moon, like the Sea of Tranquillity

explanation.surface: A grim time in the dark on the lunar surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a very unpleasant or frightening ordeal, as well as a bad dream.

clue.text: Possible lake will be in blue

indicators.note: the lake will be placed inside the other word

parts.note: blue jokes are earthy, i.e. crude
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A possible lake will be found in a blue area of a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour but means rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly, as in 'no earthly use', means conceivable or possible.

clue.text: More meagre aircrews dispersed around north

indicators.note: the scattered letters go around the single letter for north, which sits inside them
scattered aircrews have their letters spread into a new order

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Plane crews flying off northward with thinner rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' rearranges AIRCREWS into SCRAWIER, which goes 'around' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawny means thin and bony, so scrawnier is a comparative sense of being leaner or skimpier.

clue.text: Hostility's risk initially cut short

indicators.note: cut short at the start, so the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: a risk is a danger

explanation.surface: A short statement that a risk of hostility has been cut early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially cut short' drops the D from DANGER; the 's of Hostility's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a feeling of strong displeasure, the emotion behind hostility.

clue.text: Occasionally, ditches in a higher place freeze over

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then, here the second, fourth and sixth of ditches

parts.note: something placed higher is up

explanation.surface: Every so often, ditches on higher ground freeze solid.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice up is a phrasal verb for becoming coated or blocked with ice, as a surface or engine does.

clue.text: Tangled mesh, very small person's embroidery

indicators.note: something tangled is twisted out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: titch is British informal for a very small person

explanation.surface: A knotted mesh is the embroidery of some tiny person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangled' turns MESH into HEMS. TITCH is British slang for a little person; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemstitch is a decorative needlework stitch used to finish hems, a kind of embroidery.

clue.text: Document tax cheers parliamentarian blocking condemned study

indicators.note: the inserted pair sits in the way within the other letters, blocking them
a condemned building is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, like cheers
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A tax on documents prompts cheers when a politician gets in the way of a damned study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' rearranges STUDY into SDUTY, and TAMP goes inside after the S. Stamp duty is a UK tax on property and legal documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp duty is a levy charged on legal papers such as deeds and transfers.

clue.text: Aviators, ignoring the odds, race to Saturn in a frenzy

indicators.note: something in a frenzy is wildly agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order
dropping the odd letters of race to leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: Pilots defying the odds in a wild race to Saturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' leaves AEO from RACE TO; with SATURN, 'in a frenzy' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeronauts are people who travel through the air, especially balloonists, so they are aviators.

clue.text: Ham-fisted university student after drunken skinful

indicators.note: the student comes after the rearranged letters
drunken means unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A clumsy university student after a drunken skinful of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges SKINFUL into NSKILFU. A skinful is British slang for enough alcohol to get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham-fisted means clumsy or lacking in skill, which is what unskilful means.

clue.text: Sinister fish, ultimately nasty

parts.note: the shad is a herring-like fish

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word nasty

explanation.surface: A sinister fish that turns out nasty in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady describes something of doubtful honesty, suspicious or sinister in character.

clue.text: Wonder Woman, say, having drink with the Queen and her followers, essentially

parts.note: to sup is to drink
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: essentially means the very essence, here the central letter of the word followers

explanation.surface: Wonder Woman having a drink with the Queen and her retinue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes O, the central letter of FOLLOWERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonder Woman is a famous comic-book heroine with superhuman powers, an example of the type.

clue.text: Blunder in panic losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, close to panic

explanation.surface: Making a mistake because one panicked and lost one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the T from TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, which is what a blunder is.

clue.text: Analyse origin of dog from strays' enclosure?

parts.note: a dog whose origin is the pound is 'ex-pound'; ex means from
a pound is an enclosure where stray animals are kept

explanation.surface: Studying where a dog came from, asking if it was a rescue from the dog pound.
explanation.walkthrough: A rescued dog could be described as 'ex-pound', from the pound; the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to explain or set out in detail, interpreting or analysing a subject.

clue.text: Quarrel before accident involving eastern pile of junk

indicators.note: the quarrel comes first, before the rest

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or quarrel

indicators.note: the chance word wraps around the single letter, involving it

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or accident

explanation.surface: A row precedes a crash in the East, leaving a pile of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts E inside HAP to give HEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a heap of discarded scrap material, a pile of junk.

clue.text: Standard to cut whitish edible root

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: Standard instructions to trim a pale root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a cream-coloured vegetable whose long tapering root is eaten.

clue.text: Criticise military operation falsehoods — impressive collections!

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
op is short for a military operation
lies are falsehoods

explanation.surface: Slating the lies told about a military operation, with an exclamation of awe.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoply is a splendid array or full display of things, an impressive collection.

clue.text: Viral infection from India caught by 13th-century explorer

indicators.note: the letter is caught, or held, by the explorer's name around it

parts.note: Marco Polo was a Venetian traveller of the 13th century
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A medieval explorer picking up a virus in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Polio, poliomyelitis, is a disease caused by a virus that can lead to paralysis.

clue.text: Instances of promoting singular alcoholic drinks

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
ales are alcoholic drinks

explanation.surface: Marketing campaigns pushing single alcoholic drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale is an act of selling, which salespeople achieve by promoting goods.

clue.text: Men pursuing corruption in revolving bar

indicators.note: the men follow behind, pursuing the corruption

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption
OR, other ranks, is the military term for soldiers who are not officers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: Men chasing corruption in a bar that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a spinning shaft or bar.

clue.text: Suggestion of nasal intonation

definitions.meaning: a ... can be a hint or trace, as of a flavour

explanation.definitionFit: Twang means a slight tang or hint of something, and a resonant nasal sound in someone's voice.

clue.text: Regularly buys out all habitual drink

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one of buys out all

explanation.surface: A regular customer always buys the house's usual drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking for 'the usual' in a pub means ordering one's regular drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Your usual is the drink a regular customer habitually orders at a bar.

clue.text: Servile flattery about dubious deals in promising start that flops

indicators.note: the flattering word goes about, i.e. around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: to fawn is to flatter servilely; fawning is servile flattery

indicators.note: dubious means questionable, so these letters are rearranged into a doubtful order

explanation.surface: Grovelling praise surrounding shady business deals that start well and then fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' rearranges DEALS into ALSED, which FAWN goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A false dawn is an encouraging sign that comes to nothing, a hopeful beginning that fails.

clue.text: Rifle shot implodes missing aim finally

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged
missing tells us a letter is lost from the pool of letters being rearranged
finally points to the very end letter of the word aim

explanation.surface: A rifle shot implodes, having missed its target in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a gun, but here it is a verb. Take M ('aim finally') out of IMPLODES and 'shot' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack and plunder it, which is to despoil it.

clue.text: Temporary expedient to close up breach

parts.note: to stop a hole is to close it up
a breach is a gap

explanation.surface: A quick fix used to plug a breach in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a makeshift measure used until something better is available.
